newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SARFU DEFENDS PIENAAR AXING.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SARFU DEFENDS PIENAAR AXING.

text.p: The South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) on Monday defended the decision to axe Francois Pienaar, but acknowledged some top players were upset.
"I think the players are happy to abide by Andre's decision," SARFU spokesman Alex Broun said in a radio interview.
"Of course the Transvaal players and all players involved with Francois during the World Cup, many of them are hurt by the decision, I mean they've been through fire with Francois.
"But I think Andre has the complete confidence of all the players," Broun said.
He said the final verdict would come in only at the end of the tour of Argentina, France and Wales in December.
"We don't know yet whether this is a good or bad decision. Only on December 15 after the last test match in Wales will we be able to say whether it was the right decision or not."
Asked if heads would roll if the Springboks disappointed on the tour, Broun said:
"If we do not have a successful tour, that could indeed be the situation.

"But if you look at the team, it's a very strong side to play an exciting open brand of rugby and I think the direction Andre Markgraaff is moving is a very exciting direction for South African rugby, and yet there are going to be sacrifices to pay.
"But Andre must be given the chance to do what he believes is best."
Broun said there was nothing sinister in the decision to drop Pienaar and said SARFU president Louis Luyt had had nothing to do with it.
"Andre Markgraaff and the selectors have made the decision that they feel is the best interests of SA rugby. It certainly is a very tough decision.

"Andre believes that Francois would not be his first choice test loose forward and that he has better options in that position. And so if Francois is not going to be in the test team it's very difficult to take him on the tour."
